newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO AND BORDEAUX CLASH IN FRENCH LEAGUE CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO AND BORDEAUX CLASH IN FRENCH LEAGUE CLASSIC.

text.p: In-form Monaco hope history will help them beat Bordeaux in the French soccer first division on Saturday and maintain their challenge to leaders Paris St Germain.
Bordeaux have not won in the principality for 15 years and Monaco coach Jean Tigana hopes the run continues as his side are only three points behind PSG.
Tigana, who spent most of his playing career with Bordeaux, should know how difficult it is to win in the Louis II Stadium but the trend may have changed of late.
This season the Riviera side have seemed more efficient away than at home as a 1-0 defeat by Borussia Moenchengladbach in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday again showed.
"This defeat must act as a lesson. I hope it has been learnt," Tigana said.
The loss was of no consequence as Monaco had won 4-2 in Germany and Tigana now wants to concentrate on a league match which means a lot to him personally.
"I spent the eight most beautiful years of my life in Bordeaux," he said.
But there will also be a match within the match as Tigana has known Bordeaux coach Rolland Courbis since their childhood days in the suburbs of Marseille.
"We used to play against one another in high school. I can't remember who won most matches," Tigana said.
Courbis is in exactly the opposite position to that of Tigana. After a brilliant start to the season, Bordeaux were unable to win in six matches before beating Montpellier last week.
As a player, Courbis had his best results with Monaco, where he still has a house and many friends.
Bordeaux, fifth in the league and eight points behind PSG, pin their hopes on marksman Jean-Pierre Papin, another player Tigana knows well from playing with him for France and Marseille.
"Papin is a workaholic and I'm not surprised to see he's still alive and well despite all the problems he's had in recent years," Tigana said.
"I think Bordeaux are better than Moenchengladbach."

Monaco will still be without three injured internationals -- Belgian Enzo Scifo, Swiss Marco Grassi and Frenchman Eric Di Meco, who had a second knee operation last week and will not resume playing before next year.
Bordeaux will be without central defender Bernard Lambourde and left back Laurent Croci, who has a calf injury.
